blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-security-1 (Path traversal in read_attachment bypasses the ticket authorization) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Validate `name` where it enters (CWE-22): reject any name that differs from `os.path.basename(name)`, is empty, `.` or `..`, or contains a separator; better, look the name up in the `attachments` table for that `ticket_id` and refuse unknown names. Then resolve the path with `os.path.realpath` and check it stays under `os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, str(ticket_id))` before opening. Add a test that `read_attachment(agent, own_ticket, "../<other_ticket>/x")` and `read_attachment(agent, own_ticket, "/etc/passwd")` both raise.
findings.title: Path traversal in read_attachment bypasses the ticket authorization

findings.evidence:
name = os.path.basename(filename)
directory = os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, str(ticket_id))
os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
with open(os.path.join(directory, name), "wb") as f:
findings.recommendation: Store each upload under a server-generated name (for example a UUID, kept in the `attachments` row next to the display name), or open with mode `"xb"` and refuse or rename on collision. Keep the client's file name only as display metadata.
findings.title: An upload silently overwrites an existing attachment of the same name

findings.evidence: def save_attachment(ticket_id: int, filename: str, data: bytes) -> str:
findings.recommendation: Take the caller's `agent_id` and check `may_read_ticket` (or a dedicated write permission) before writing, as `read_attachment` does, so the operation is authorized server-side wherever it is called from.
findings.title: save_attachment takes no caller identity, so it enforces no authorization

findings.evidence:
with open(os.path.join(directory, name), "wb") as f:
    f.write(data)
findings.recommendation: Enforce a maximum size and an allow-list of accepted types (by extension and sniffed content) where the upload enters, and refuse the rest before writing.
findings.title: Uploaded data has no size or type limit
